title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
description: Learn how to extend Claude's capabilities by connecting it to external data sources and tools using the Model Context Protocol.
learning_objectives: Explain the architecture of MCP including Hosts, Clients, and Servers
Install and configure a pre-built MCP server in Claude Desktop
Utilize MCP Resources to provide the model with external context
Execute MCP Tools to perform actions in external systems
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with JSON configuration files

sections.heading: Introduction to Model Context Protocol
sections.content_brief: Explain MCP as an open standard that replaces fragmented integrations. Discuss the core problem it solves: giving LLMs a standardized way to access data and tools without custom glue code for every application.

sections.heading: The MCP Architecture
sections.content_brief: Break down the three-tier architecture: the MCP Host (e.g., Claude Desktop), the MCP Client, and the MCP Server. Explain how they communicate via a standardized protocol to exchange resources and tools.

sections.heading: Configuring Your First MCP Server
sections.content_brief: Walk through the process of adding a server to the Claude Desktop configuration file. Demonstrate how to add a community server (like the filesystem or GitHub server) by editing the JSON config.
sections.code_context: Example of a claude_desktop_config.json file adding a filesystem and github server

sections.heading: Working with MCP Resources
sections.content_brief: Define 'Resources' as read-only data sources (like files, database schemas, or API docs). Show how Claude identifies available resources and pulls them into the conversation context.
sections.code_context: Example of a prompt requesting a specific MCP resource by URI

sections.heading: Executing MCP Tools
sections.content_brief: Define 'Tools' as executable functions that allow the model to take actions (e.g., creating a Jira ticket or querying a DB). Explain the loop of tool discovery, call generation, and result processing.
sections.code_context: Example interaction where Claude uses an MCP tool to fetch data from an external API

admonitions.content: Be cautious when installing third-party MCP servers. Since these servers can have access to your local filesystem or API keys, only use servers from trusted sources.
You can find a growing list of community-maintained MCP servers on GitHub and the official Anthropic documentation to extend Claude's reach into your existing toolstack.
